\ubblockdescription{catalogue.multiscale_entropy}{A complexity fingerprint per window: the signal is blurred more and more (averaged over 1 s, 2 s, ... minutes) and at every blur the block asks how surprising the next value is (sample entropy; Costa, Goldberger \& Peng 2005, refined composite form). White noise loses its surprise as it is blurred; a signal with structure at many time-scales keeps it --- the curve's shape is the fingerprint. It needs hours per curve, so it describes recordings, species and conditions, not events. Coloured noise has a curve of its own, so judge a curve against amplitude-adjusted (aaft) copies of the same recording (Surrogate generator, method aaft) --- not plain phase-randomised ones, which also change the value distribution this measure reads, so a non-Gaussian recording would beat them on its distribution alone. Tune scale\_max\_s first (the coarsest blur; long windows reach further). An undetrended recording collapses the curve towards 0 (drift inflates r); the block flags it --- detrend upstream.}

  \ubparam{scale\_\allowbreak{}max\_\allowbreak{}s}{1200.0}{number, at least 0.001}{Tune this first --- the coarsest blur, in seconds (default 20 min, the plan's). A scale needs min\_coarse\_len averaged points, so a window of W seconds reaches about W / min\_coarse\_len: a 24 h window at the default \textasciitilde{}86 s, a 72 h window \textasciitilde{}4 min, a whole 721 h channel \textasciitilde{}43 min. Scales beyond the reach are blank, and said so.}%
  \ubparam{scale\_\allowbreak{}min\_\allowbreak{}s}{1.0}{number, at least 0.001}{The finest scale, in seconds (one sample at 1 Hz).}%
  \ubparam{n\_\allowbreak{}scales}{12}{whole number from 1 to 60}{How many scales, spaced evenly on a log axis between the two (block sizes that round to the same number of samples are merged).}%
  \ubparam{r\_\allowbreak{}frac}{0.15}{number from 0.01 to 1}{The match tolerance r as a fraction of the window's spread (the paper's 0.15; it suggests 0.10-0.20). Larger r: more matches, lower entropy everywhere.}%
  \ubparam{r\_\allowbreak{}scale}{\texttt{mad}}{one of \texttt{mad}, \texttt{sd}}{The spread r is taken from, once per window and fixed across scales: mad (1.4826 \ensuremath{\times} the median absolute deviation --- robust to outliers and to the events themselves) or sd (Costa's standard deviation --- inflated by drift and outliers, which makes entropy collapse).}%
  \ubparam{method}{\texttt{rcmse}}{one of \texttt{rcmse}, \texttt{mse}}{rcmse (refined composite, Wu et al. 2014 as restated by Azami et al. 2017: pools the matches of every offset, so fewer scales are undefined on short series) or mse (Costa 2005's original, for fidelity checks).}%
  \ubparam{m}{2}{whole number from 1 to 3}{Template length (the paper's 2).}%
  \ubparam{min\_\allowbreak{}coarse\_\allowbreak{}len}{1000}{whole number, at least 10}{A scale whose averaged series is shorter than this is blank (Costa's section VI kept 1,000 points at its coarsest scale). Lowering it reaches coarser scales with noisier, biased values; no lower default has been measured.}%
  \ubparam{max\_\allowbreak{}points}{20000}{whole number from 1000 to 200000}{Cost cap: each averaged series is scored on at most this many templates (Costa's N), taken from 10 stretches spread across the window, so every scale costs about the same. Raise it for a steadier estimate at the cost of time (the work grows as its square).}%
  \ubparam{max\_\allowbreak{}gap\_\allowbreak{}s}{30.0}{number from 0 to 86400}{Missing-sample runs up to this long are bridged by straight lines; a window with a longer run is left out (a blank row), counted, as is a window more than 5 \% filled. Both are placeholders, not measured.}%
  \ubparam{inflation\_\allowbreak{}limit}{1.5}{number from 1 to 100}{The collapse guard: a window's spread as it arrives over its spread after a 2 h rolling mean is taken out. Above this, drift or outliers inflated r and every scale of the window is flagged (its entropy is low for a reason that is not the signal's).
